DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM (deviation-analysis-memo)
Matter: PBPEPS side letter SL-RGEF4-PBPEPS-001 (June 15, 2022) v. Ridgeline Growth Equity Fund IV, L.P. A&R LPA (June 15, 2022); CIO's IC approval memo. Governing law: Delaware (LPA 13.1). Prepared on the documents only; the Delaware citations below are unverified (the statute site was blocked).

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) The controlling gate is LPA 13.5(b) (repeated in 14.2(d)): a side letter overrides the LPA only where it contains express "notwithstanding" language overriding identified LPA provisions; otherwise the LPA governs and the side letter is "supplemental to, and not in derogation of" it. Side Letter Sections 5(a) (LPAC seat), 6 (key person) and 7 (clawback) say "In addition to", not "notwithstanding", and each conflicts with an LPA provision. Section 9 (withdrawal) has no override of LPA 3.1(b) (irrevocable commitments). These four headline protections are at serious risk of being unenforceable, yet the IC memo presents them as binding concessions.
(b) The IC memo misstates the side letter in at least five places (co-investment threshold, withdrawal threshold, clawback "notwithstanding" language, MFN scope, and omissions in Section 8). The IC was asked to approve on a summary that does not match the document.
(c) Several drafting errors need a corrective amendment (Side Letter 11(a): signed writing by both parties).
Caveat: the side letter copy has blank signature lines and the memo describes a "draft"; confirm the executed version.

2. DEVIATION TABLE (LPA baseline / Side Letter / effect / IC memo accuracy)

1. Management fee (LPA 4.1; SL 1). LPA 1.75% of commitment during Investment Period (to June 14, 2027), 1.50% of invested capital after. SL 1.50% / 1.25%, with "Notwithstanding 4.1". LPA 4.1(g) expressly permits side-letter fee terms. EFFECTIVE. Math checks: $2,625,000 v. $3,062,500; $437,500 a year; $2,187,500 over five years. Memo's "$4,375,000" total is a ceiling that assumes the full $175M stays invested for five post-period years and ignores the 100% fee offset (4.1(f)), which SL expressly preserves, and the two possible term extensions. Memo basically accurate; label as maximum, not estimate.

2. MFN (LPA 10.2; SL 2). Has "Notwithstanding 10.2", so effective. Deviations: (i) notice 15 days after Final Close (Oct 15, 2022) v. LPA 30 days (Oct 30, 2022); election 90 v. 60 days; election effective from admission v. LPA later of side-letter date/election, prospective. These favor PBPEPS. (ii) Adverse to PBPEPS and not flagged by memo: SL limits electable terms to LPs with commitments equal to or below $175M; LPA 10.2 has no size limit for an MFN Eligible LP (>= $150M). Because SL overrides "anything to the contrary", the SL arguably narrows PBPEPS's LPA rights. Fix: add "in addition to, not in limitation of, LPA 10.2". Calendar status: windows closed long ago (by early 2023); confirm whether notice was received and an election made, since LPA 10.2(e) supplemental-notice rights (30 days) may remain.

3. Co-investment (no LPA analogue; SL 3). SL threshold: fund equity commitment above $125,000,000; allocation up to ~6.29% of the excess (true figure 6.295%, LPA Sch. A); no fee/no carry; 10-business-day response window. IC memo says $100,000,000 (twice). MISSTATEMENT: at $200M deal, SL yields about $4.72M (confirmed arithmetic) v. about $6.29M at a $100M threshold. Also: SL 3 is expressly "subject to" GP fiduciary and legal constraints, and requires only "commercially reasonable efforts" on timing, so the right is weaker than "co-invest rights" implies. No fund-level conflict (LPA is silent), but because LPA 10.2(d)(iii) excludes co-investment from other LPs' MFN, no MFN leakage.

4. Reporting (LPA 7.1; SL 10(a)). "Notwithstanding 7.1" so effective. Quarterly 60 days (v. 90), audited annual 90 days (v. 120), plus monthly portfolio summaries within 30 days. But SL obliges only "commercially reasonable efforts" and excuses delay for circumstances beyond GP control, so the timelines are soft; the memo presents them as firm. Note the K-1 date (LPA 7.1(c), 90 days) is unchanged and cannot practically follow 90-day audit comfortably. SL quarterly list omits statement of changes in partners' capital but is "in addition to" 7.1, so no loss.

5. LPAC seat (LPA 8.1; SL 5(a)). LPA 8.1(a)-(c): GP's sole discretion; GP may remove any member at any time (8.1(b)); "No LP shall have the right to demand appointment" and the agreement "does not provide for any automatic appointment, guaranteed seat, or other mandatory LPAC membership right". SL 5(a) says "In addition to" 8.1, no override, and promises a seat "for the term of the Fund". Direct conflict, LPA 13.5(b) not satisfied: seat likely unenforceable as against the LPA; at most a contractual damages claim against the GP under the side letter, which the GP will say is "supplemental" only and defeated by 8.1(c). HIGH RISK. IC memo and counsel's note call the seat "guaranteed" without addressing 8.1(c) or 13.5(b). Fix: amendment with "Notwithstanding Sections 8.1(b) and (c)".

6. Key person (LPA 6.3; SL 6). Same Key Person Event definition (Ridgeline plus two of three SMDs; 75% time test). LPA 6.3(c): suspension only upon 60% LP vote; 180-day cure; permanent termination if uncured and suspended unless 75% reinstates. SL: automatic suspension, no vote; follow-on cap of 15% of Commitments (matches LPA 6.1(b)(i)); resumes on replacement "reasonably acceptable to the Investor" or 60% LP vote. No "notwithstanding"; conflicts with 6.3(c). LIKELY UNENFORCEABLE under 13.5(b). IC memo's description ("stronger protection; no reliance on LP vote") is wrong as a matter of enforceability. Recommend deleting as drafted and replacing with a PBPEPS-specific right (e.g., notice and a right to be excused from further calls or to withdraw during any Key Person Event), which affects only PBPEPS.

7. Clawback (LPA 5.3; SL 7). LPA 5.3(b): net of taxes at assumed 45%; 5.3(c): personal guaranties (net basis); 5.3(e): 30% escrow; 5.3(a): amounts returned to the FUND for distribution to LPs. SL 7 says "In addition to", yet purports to apply gross, "notwithstanding" nothing; the IC memo says "notwithstanding the LPA" - false. Without override language, 5.3(b) governs. Further defects: (i) clawback under LPA runs to the Fund, not to an individual LP "dollar-for-dollar", so per-LP gross treatment is structurally mismatched and would need a waterfall/true-up mechanism; (ii) SL cites escrow "Section 5.3(c)", but escrow is 5.3(e) (5.3(c) is guaranty), and escrow is only 30% of carry, so the claim that escrow is "sufficient" for a gross obligation is unsupported and the personal guaranties remain net; Value: memo's illustration ($10M excess -> $5.5M v. $10M) overstates the benefit as PBPEPS's share would be about 6.295% of the Fund's recovery in any event. HIGH RISK; cure by amendment with "Notwithstanding 5.3(b) and (c)", pro rata mechanics, and a guaranty gross-up.

8. Transfers (LPA 9.1; SL 4). "Notwithstanding 9.1": effective as to GP consent, minimum size and transfer fees. Open issues: LPA 9.1(b) bars transferees that are not qualified purchasers/accredited investors, any Competitor, or that cause adverse regulatory consequences, and is itself introduced "Notwithstanding any other provision". SL does not clearly displace it; a governmental-plan transferee that is not a QP could be blocked, and the SL 4(c)(iii) opinion on the Investment Company Act is at PBPEPS's cost. Also LPA 9.1(e) cost-shifting is overridden only for "transfer fee or administrative charge", not the GP's legal costs; SL 4(d) refers to ERISA, which does not apply to a governmental plan (drafting oddity). SL's 30-day notice, assumption and opinion conditions are omitted from the IC memo (which mentions only the opinion).

9. Excuse rights (LPA 9.2; SL 5(b)). "Notwithstanding 9.2": effective. SL excuses for (i) Government Code violations (tobacco, firearms, thermal coal) and (ii) portfolio companies with over 15% revenue from those sectors, even though LPA 9.2(a), (f) bar policy-based excuses. Memo says the right protects "Board-adopted ESG policies"; the SL clause (ii) is policy-based, and the SL override covers it, but the GP may argue (i) is the only statutory basis.The cited statutory scope (Gov. Code 7500-7914) was not verified; confirm specific statutes and whether they extend to private-fund holdings.

10. Confidentiality / CPRA (LPA 10.1; SL 10(b)). "Notwithstanding 10.1": effective. GP will not designate information confidential to impede CPRA disclosure except trade secrets (Civ. Code 3426.1) and portfolio-company information; log within 30 days; PBPEPS gives 10 business days' notice. Fine in substance. Notes: CPRA was recodified effective January 1, 2023 (now Gov. Code 7920.000 et seq.; the former 6250 reference should be read accordingly), and the fund-records exemption (former 6254.26, now 7928.710) should be checked against the side letter; both unverified here. SL 11(f) confidentiality of side letter terms yields to CPRA. The IC memo's reading (consistent) is acceptable.

11. Withdrawal (LPA 3.1(b), 11.2; SL 9). LPA: irrevocable "except as expressly provided in this Agreement". SL grants withdrawal without penalty if 50% of aggregate commitments ($1.39B of $2.78B) is not deployed by June 15, 2025; election period June 15 - August 14, 2025; 90 days' irrevocable notice; NAV paid within 180 days. IC memo says 40% - MISSTATEMENT (SL is more favorable). No "notwithstanding" language overriding 3.1(b) or 11.2; LPA 13.5(b) problem. Conflicts with 14.1(d) as a withdrawal reduces fund capital and the denominator for every other LP (SL says others not required to fund more, but excused/forfeited amounts reduce their liquidity and fee base and the subscription facility collateral under 3.2(d)-(e)). Also the lender's security interest (3.2(e)) is not addressed. TIMING: the window has closed (current date October 2, 2026); unless a notice was timely delivered, the right has lapsed (SL 9, "no further force or effect"). Determine whether deployment passed the threshold at June 15, 2025, whether any notice was sent, and whether the right was enforceable. Also "within 60 days" is 61 days by SL dates.

12. Exculpation / indemnification (LPA 12.1, 12.2; SL 8). "Notwithstanding 12.1 and 12.2": effective as drafting, and LPA 12.2(d) allows a different standard by side letter "subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement". SL removes exculpation for negligence for claims by or for PBPEPS and limits Fund indemnity for negligence (judgment or arbitral award). Under Delaware law an LPA may modify or eliminate duties and liabilities subject to the implied covenant (6 Del. C. 17-1101(d), (f), unverified); a side letter is contract-based, but the following limit value: (i) the GP's 12.3(a) liability cap ($55.6M) is not overridden and arguably caps recovery; The memo omits 8(b)-(c) and the breadth ("any investment decision" in pooled investments). Moderate risk; indemnification interplay with the GP-LPAC member indemnity in 12.1(a) is also untouched.

3. DOCUMENT AND PROCESS ERRORS
- SL 11(e) cites notices at "Section 13.4"; notices are in LPA 13.3 (13.4 is successors).
- SL 7 cites escrow at 5.3(c); correct is 5.3(e).
- Counsel names: SL letterhead "Graystone Kirkland LLP"; LPA and IC memo "Graystone Hargrove LLP" (LPA 13.3 email domain is graystonekirkland.com); correct.
- GP signatory titled "Managing Partner" in SL and "Managing Member" in LPA; confirm authority.

4. RANKED RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Within weeks: seek a written amendment (SL 11(a)) restating Sections 5(a), 6, 7 and 9 with express "notwithstanding Sections ..." language naming 8.1(b)-(c), 6.3(c)-(e), 5.3(b)-(c), 3.1(b); alternatively obtain GP written confirmation that it will honour them. Where the term touches other LPs (key person, withdrawal), obtain 14.1 consent or redesign as PBPEPS-only rights.
2. Report to the IC the true terms (co-investment $125M, withdrawal 50%, clawback "in addition to", MFN size cap) and the enforceability gap; ask for ratification. 
3. Pull the GP's MFN notice, any election, and the 2025 deployment data; confirm whether the withdrawal right was exercised or lapsed.
4. Correct cross-references and counsel name in the amendment.

Freedom of contract in LP agreements (unverified; fetch blocked)
